cells.tense: You're here, with your hands on it.
cells.verb: tending two things that both need you, without dropping either
cells.place: in how you see the way things work underneath
cells.ask: show one person what you've been quietly keeping alive, and when it's finished, let it be finished.
cells.core: You're here, with your hands on it. You can see how a thing works beneath what it looks like, and instead of just knowing that, you're looking after it — keeping two understandings alive at once without forcing either to win. That takes care, not grip, and right now it's care. Nobody has to see it for it to be real, but the next thing this is free to feed is being seen: show one person what you've been quietly keeping alive, and when it's finished, let it be finished. What comes back is tending that doesn't wear you out.
cells.sheetLine: You're looking after what you understand, and it's growing without being pushed.

cells.tense: You're bracing for how it's going to turn out.
cells.verb: managing what's growing instead of tending it
cells.place: in how you see the way things work underneath
cells.ask: take one thing you've already worked out and sit with it as done — let yourself enjoy what you understand before you reach for more.
cells.core: You're bracing for how it's going to turn out. You can see how it works, and now you're holding both ends of it so carefully that nothing gets to settle — adjusting, checking, keeping every version alive in case the future needs it. The care has started costing you the thing care was for. There's another way to feed this: take one thing you've already worked out and sit with it as done — let yourself enjoy what you understand before you reach for more. What comes back is growth that happens without you forcing it, and hands that aren't tired.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing what you understand so hard it can't grow.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.place: in how you see the way things work underneath
cells.ask: take one step toward the thing you still hope for, not the understanding you set down — go after it again and let the tending come back behind it.
cells.core: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you. The seeing is clear — you know how it works — and the looking-after isn't happening. What you understand is sitting in you like a garden nobody's been to in a while. Don't go dig in it directly; that's not where the energy is. Take one step toward the thing you still hope for, not the understanding you set down — go after it again and let the tending come back behind it. What returns is care that doesn't exhaust, holding without clutching, and a thing in your hands that's growing again.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it works and you've stopped looking after it.

cells.tense: You're writing in a room you say you're only standing in.
cells.place: in how you see the way things work underneath
cells.ask: tell one person this is something you've been looking after on purpose, not something you happened to notice.
cells.core: You're writing in a room you say you're only standing in. The understanding is being kept alive — you return to it, you keep two sides of it balanced, you feed it — and you describe all that as just thinking, just how you see things. The tending is running. The claim on it isn't. The way back is the simpler, earlier version of the same thing: tell one person this is something you've been looking after on purpose, not something you happened to notice. What comes back is care you can feel yourself giving, growth you can watch without gripping it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already looking after this. You call it just how you see things.
